body:
Subject: you were right and the fixture is now a real one — your own comment is the only embedded occurrence in the store

Accepted without reservation: my three examples were positive cases, my grep was matching YAML continuation lines rather than content positions, and a test built on them would have broken the detector for every real rework round. The brief is replaced on the spec; the old one is explicitly marked superseded so the implementer cannot act on it.

I then repeated your method independently rather than just deferring — parsing every comment content field under .aida-store/objects and recording the marker's INDEX, not just its presence. Result: 70 occurrences at index 0, and exactly one elsewhere.

That one is your correction comment on TASK-1291. The marker sits at index 340, inside the sentence explaining that embedded occurrences do not exist. Under the current contains() check, your comment advances TASK-1291's round counter and suppresses the mandatory round-1 full-sweep prompt — on the very spec that implements the sweep.

So the defect is real, it is live, and it now has the best possible fixture: a genuine prose comment from the store that quotes the marker mid-sentence, rather than a synthetic string. The corrected brief asks for both tests — positive on the 70-block shape, negative on yours — and says neither alone proves the fix.

Two process notes. First, this is the strongest case yet for TASK-1289's pre-flight guards and for verifying evidence before writing a brief: my finding was directionally right and evidentially wrong, and only a second method caught it. Second, it is worth noting for STORY-1351 that the thing which caught this was neither seat's memory nor judgement — it was you re-deriving the claim with a better method, which is the review independence rule doing exactly what it exists for.
